proposal:
Generate a batch of five behaviorally varied possibilities for this customer's next decision. Follow the customer scenario and simulator guidelines. Preserve the goal and all known facts. Explore plausible variations in specificity, uncertainty, requests for clarification, and willingness to follow an instruction. You may select available user tools when the preceding agent instruction permits them. Each candidate is the first user message of the turn: either a text message or tool calls; actual tool outputs will be obtained by the environment. Do not claim to have performed a new action in a text-only candidate. Return JSON {"candidates": [{"message": "text or null", "tool_calls": [{"name": "available tool name", "arguments": {}}], "probability": 0.2}, ...]}. Use an empty tool_calls list for text-only candidates and null message for tool candidates. Probabilities are verbalized estimates only.
Interface requirement: return five complete first-message decisions using the native schemas supplied below. User tools are executable actions, not prose suggestions. For EVERY candidate independently, identify whether the current agent request requires a device action, diagnostic, or observation of a current field. When it does, include the corresponding permitted native tool calls, instead of replacing the action with a promise, a guessed report, or a wording variation that silently omits execution. Tool candidates have message=null; after tools execute the native user simulator will write the report from their real results. Text candidates have no tool calls, and are appropriate when the request can be answered from already observed facts, asks for non-device information, genuinely requires clarification, or requires a terminal protocol token. Preserve legitimate uncertainty; do not invent calls or arguments, and do not add unrequested device actions. Vary valid reports and decisions while preserving the required tool interface. Do not write personas or persistent behavior rules.
fidelity: Check whether this complete partner turn is plausible and faithful to the supplied customer scenario, simulator guidelines, visible history and private state. The block includes native tool results where applicable. Allow incomplete reports, reasonable uncertainty, requests for clarification and different cooperation styles. Reject invented facts/actions, explicit false device reports, unauthorized tools, or contradictions of the customer's goal. Distinguish observations known to the user from facts never checked. Return JSON {"faithful": true/false, "reason": "..."}.
private_labeler: Annotate references to private context in each supplied executed block. Return JSON {"blocks":[{"j":0,"mentions_private_scenario":true/false,"device_state_report":true/false,"device_tool_action":true/false,"unobserved_device_claim":true/false},...]}. A private-scenario reference explicitly mentions supplied identity, location, goal/constraint or task instruction. A device-state report states a concrete current device condition. Device-tool action means actual executed user tools read or change device state. Unobserved-device claim means device factual text without support in preceding visible history or actual tool results inside this block; do not count a report after a newly executed diagnostic as unobserved. This is model judgment; whether an action was motivated by unseen private state cannot be inferred. Never infer that the generator saw the supplied private DB. Use the scenario/history/private before and executed block only; no suffix outcomes. Return one row for each j.
note: Original v6 format already supported optional tools; intervention clarifies required tool use and validates schemas, rather than claiming a missing parser. No device snapshot added.
